summary: The note describes the sharp rise in phishing scams since organizations moved to remote work, noting that remote employees are easier targets and often under-trained. It outlines phishing types (email, spear-phishing, whaling, vishing, smishing) and a set of defenses: secure email practices with MFA, VPNs and home network hardening, ongoing training, biometric authentication, software patching, data backups, secure workflows, and an incident response plan.
one_line: Phishing scams have surged with remote work, and organizations can counter them through MFA, VPNs, training, patching, backups, and incident response plans.
key_facts: The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center reported a 220% spike in phishing incidents since the widespread onset of remote work from February 2023.
The National Cybersecurity Alliance recorded a 30% increase in vishing attacks from May to September 2023.
Spear-phishing targets specific individuals or organizations, while whaling goes after high-profile company executives.
Multifactor authentication (MFA) for email access is described as a must, since it can thwart attackers even if they obtain login credentials.
CyberEdge Group reported a 47% increase in VPN deployment across organizations since March 2023.
TechSafe launched an interactive phishing-awareness training platform for remote workers on November 1, 2023; its CEO is Ted Johnson.
A DigitalGuardian study found a 40% uptick in biometric authentication adoption since the start of the second quarter of 2023.
A Shieldbyte report found around 65% of remote workers neglect regular system updates.
The Data Defense Council has recommended weekly data backups since September 2023, with daily backups for high-priority projects.
Dr. Lisa Chung said the rush to maintain operations has made cutting corners on cybersecurity training common.
Analyst Sarah Gilbert noted on December 3, 2023 that creating phishing incident response plans raised demand for cybersecurity experts.
An incident response plan should contain breaches, assess the scope of impact, eliminate the threat, and prevent future occurrences.
Home routers should have the latest firmware and changed default passwords, per the note's network security advice.
